solved.q: The work function of a metal is 2 eV. Find (i) the threshold frequency and (ii) the threshold wavelength for the metal. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
steps: Formula: phi0 = h v0, so v0 = phi0 / h.
Formula for threshold wavelength: lambda0 = h c / phi0.

solved.topic: Einstein's photoelectric equation - KEmax and vmax
solved.q: Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal surface of work function 2 eV. Find (i) the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons in eV and (ii) their maximum velocity. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, me = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
steps: Given: lambda = 400 x 10^-9 m, phi0 = 2 eV, h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s, me = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg.
Formula: v = c / lambda, then Einstein's equation h v = phi0 + KEmax.
Formula: KEmax = (1/2) me vmax^2, so vmax = sqrt(2 KEmax / me).
Substitution: vmax = sqrt(2 x 1.78 x 10^-19 / 9.1 x 10^-31) = sqrt(3.91 x 10^11).

solved.q: Light of frequency 6 x 10^14 Hz falls on a metal surface of work function 1.9 eV. Calculate the stopping potential. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
steps: Formula: e V0 = h v - phi0, so V0 = (h v - phi0) / e.
Converting to eV: h v = 3.978 x 10^-19 / 1.6 x 10^-19 = 2.49 eV.
V0 = (2.49 - 1.9) eV / e = 0.59 V (since energy in eV divided by e in units of e gives volts directly).

solved.topic: Finding Planck's constant and work function from V0-v graph
solved.q: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential was found to be 1.0 V at frequency 6 x 10^14 Hz and 1.5 V at frequency 7.5 x 10^14 Hz. Using the straight line graph of V0 versus v, find (i) Planck's constant and (ii) the work function of the metal, given e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C.
steps: Formula: e V0 = h v - phi0, which is a straight line V0 = (h/e) v - (phi0/e), so slope = h/e = (V02 - V01)/(v2 - v1).

solved.topic: De Broglie wavelength of an accelerated electron
solved.q: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V. Find its de Broglie wavelength. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, me = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
steps: Formula: lambda = h / sqrt(2 me e V).

solved.q: Find the de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron moving with a speed of 1.0 x 10^6 m/s. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, me = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
steps: Substitution: me v = 9.1 x 10^-31 x 1.0 x 10^6 = 9.1 x 10^-25 kg m/s.

solved.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a macroscopic body
solved.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a ball of mass 0.1 kg moving with a speed of 10 m/s. Comment on the result. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s)
steps: Substitution: m v = 0.1 x 10 = 1 kg m/s.
This wavelength is extremely small compared to the size of the ball, so the wave nature of the ball is not observable.

solved.topic: Photon energy, momentum and photon flux of a laser
solved.q: A laser of power 1 mW emits light of wavelength 600 nm. Find (i) the energy of each photon in eV, (ii) the momentum of each photon, and (iii) the number of photons emitted per second. (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
steps: Formula: E = h c / lambda; momentum p = h / lambda = E / c; number of photons per second n = P / E.
Calculation: E = 3.315 x 10^-19 J = 2.07 eV (dividing by 1.6 x 10^-19).
